title: Brown's electrometers pick up anomalies matching the sidereal calendar, run up to the end of his life on Catalina
summary: Linda Brown tells of Brown's electrometers pick up anomalies matching the sidereal calendar, run up to the end of his life on Catalina, about lifelong, up to 1985 at Santa Catalina Island, California, and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: One of the things he did was build these devices that he called electrometers and they were receiving maybe neutrinos.

plain: Linda Brown says on Jesse Michels's podcast that the scientist Townsend Brown built devices he called electrometers, which she says may have been picking up neutrinos, tiny particles that pass through almost everything. According to the telling, he kept them running until the end of his life on Catalina Island, California, in 1985, and they recorded oddities that followed the sidereal calendar, meaning time measured by the stars rather than the Sun. If true, it would point to some unknown influence coming from space.
